newsitem.title: UK: Grampian takes control of Edinburgh Woollen.
newsitem.headline: Grampian takes control of Edinburgh Woollen.

text.p: Grampian Holdings Plc said it was buying the 75 percent of The Edinburgh Woollen Mill that it did not already own for 64.4 million stg.
It said it would make a one-for-five rights issue at 125 pence per share to raise 14.8 million stg.
It added it would also buy Scottish Woollens Group for five million stg.

Grampian is offering one stg in cash plus one share for each Edinburgh Woollen Mill (EWM) "A' share, and EWM shareholders will also be entitled to receive a second interim dividend of 2.67p. It has acceptances for 92 percent of the EWM "A' shares.
Grampian also announced an 11 percent rise in half-year pre-tax profit to 4.75 million pounds and an eight percent rise in its dividend to 1.95p.
EWM will form a new retail division within Grampian. EWM chairman and managing director, David Stevenson and Colin Birrell, will join the Grampian board, with Setevenson as group deputy chairman.
"This is a rare opportunity to expand the group, affording excellent prospects for sustained growth," Grampian chairman Bill Hughes said in a statement.
The company said it plans an analysts meeting on the moves at 0900 GMT, at the offices of Financial Dynamics in London.
